provenance: First published in 1908 under the name Three Initiates, The Kybalion is a modern Hermetic-inspired work associated with New Thought writer William Walker Atkinson. Its seven-principle system is not authenticated ancient Egyptian teaching. Here it serves as a philosophical and artistic lens. Urban exercises are contemporary CAISIK interpretations; sound and visual experiments do not prove metaphysical claims.

principles.name: Mentalism
principles.subtitle: Change the lens.
principles.doctrine: The book presents reality as fundamentally mental.
principles.context: A metaphysical claim within its idealist worldview.
principles.explanation: For this exercise, explore how attention changes your experience of a place. A camera sees a wall; memory may see home, exclusion, or possibility.
principles.urban: Read one façade through three lenses: architect, resident, writer.
principles.observe: Which details emerge when your purpose changes?
principles.exercise: Describe the same street once as a stranger, then as someone returning home.
principles.freestyle: Four bars. One location. Two conflicting inner voices.
principles.artwork: An engraved eye whose iris becomes a street grid.
principles.demo: Switch between architecture, memory, and creative possibility annotations on the same unchanged image.
principles.deeper: Compare your descriptions. Name an assumption that changed.

principles.name: Correspondence
principles.subtitle: Find the echo.
principles.doctrine: It proposes analogies between different levels of existence.
principles.context: Analogy functions as a method of interpretation.
principles.explanation: A branching road can resemble a branching thought. The resemblance can inspire art without proving that both share a hidden cause.
principles.urban: Compare a rose window, a street intersection, and a graffiti letter.
principles.observe: Find repetition, symmetry, and one deliberate disruption.
principles.exercise: Sketch a detail, then a larger structure with a similar pattern. Record one important difference.
principles.freestyle: Connect a crack in stone to a crack in certainty.
principles.artwork: Two rotating architectural rosettes linked across a horizontal axis.
principles.demo: Compare a window pattern and an abstract city network at different scales. Label the comparison visual analogy.
principles.deeper: Write where the analogy becomes misleading.

principles.name: Vibration
principles.subtitle: Listen beneath the surface.
principles.doctrine: It describes existence through differing states of motion.
principles.context: Its spiritual extension of vibration is metaphysical.
principles.explanation: Use actual sound as your creative material. A train or gate can inspire a composition; it does not establish spiritual frequencies.
principles.urban: Listen to shutters, footsteps, ventilation, and passing transport.
principles.observe: Separate a continuous sound from a sudden one.
principles.exercise: Make a written sound inventory, or record an environment where recording is permitted.
principles.freestyle: Turn three city sounds into three recurring phrases.
principles.artwork: Fine concentric rings intersected by a waveform.
principles.demo: Adjust an oscillator frequency and hear the pitch after pressing Play. Label this a sound experiment, not metaphysical evidence.
principles.deeper: Describe how your composition changes when one sound disappears.

principles.name: Polarity
principles.subtitle: Work the space between.
principles.doctrine: It treats opposites as differing degrees of one quality.
principles.context: The text uses this to discuss mental transformation.
principles.explanation: Use contrast to expand a description. A place can hold beauty and neglect together. This artistic lens does not make every opposition equivalent.
principles.urban: Photograph the threshold between sunlight and shade.
principles.observe: Find a transition rather than only two extremes.
principles.exercise: Choose polished/raw, crowded/quiet, or familiar/strange. Describe three intermediate states.
principles.freestyle: Begin in anger; change your language toward curiosity by the fourth bar.
principles.artwork: A divided disc with a continuous gold-to-obsidian transition.
principles.demo: Move a contrast slider across an architectural image with changing descriptive words, never moral scores.
principles.deeper: Name something this spectrum cannot adequately describe.

principles.name: Rhythm
principles.subtitle: Leave room for the return.
principles.doctrine: It describes recurring movements between contrasting states.
principles.context: Its pendulum image extends into human experience.
principles.explanation: Explore repetition and variation as compositional tools. A repeated column or returning rhyme creates expectation; a pause can interrupt it.
principles.urban: Read columns as a beat and doorways as rests.
principles.observe: Find a regular pattern and its interruption.
principles.exercise: Tap a comfortable pulse. Speak a short phrase, leave a beat empty, then answer it.
principles.freestyle: Deliver four bars with straight timing, then with deliberate pauses.
principles.artwork: A pendulum crossing a restrained four-step beat grid.
principles.demo: Start a four-beat metronome, adjust BPM, and mute steps. Include Stop and silent visual mode.
principles.deeper: Listen back. Identify one pause that makes the meaning clearer.

principles.name: Cause and Effect
principles.subtitle: Trace the consequence.
principles.doctrine: It places events within an all-encompassing chain of causation.
principles.context: This is the book's deterministic philosophical position.
principles.explanation: Trace an observable sequence and distinguish evidence from a guessed cause. A stain can be visible while its origin remains unknown.
principles.urban: Follow how a building alteration changes movement around an entrance.
principles.observe: Which consequence can you see? Which cause needs a source?
principles.exercise: Write a three-step chain. Mark each link observed, documented, or uncertain.
principles.freestyle: Sixteen bars: action, consequence, response, changed direction.
principles.artwork: An engraved branching chain of connected nodes.
principles.demo: Change an input in a fictional foot-traffic model and observe its stated rules. Show its assumptions.
principles.deeper: Add an alternative cause. What evidence would distinguish them?

principles.name: Gender
principles.subtitle: Receive. Initiate. Create.
principles.doctrine: It uses masculine/feminine categories to explain generation.
principles.context: These are historically gendered metaphysical categories.
principles.explanation: Our adaptation explores receiving and initiating as creative modes available to everyone. We do not assign these modes to sexes, identities, or social roles.
principles.urban: Notice the relationship between a courtyard and the activity within it.
principles.observe: What does the space invite, and what does a visitor introduce?
principles.exercise: Collect impressions for one minute, then transform them into a sketch or phrase.
principles.freestyle: Alternate a bar that listens to the city with a bar that answers.
principles.artwork: Two distinct interweaving lines forming a new central shape.
principles.demo: Combine two independent patterns into a third composition. Label the controls Receive and Initiate; avoid male/female person icons.
principles.deeper: Identify which creative mode you used first, and reverse the order.

freestyleExercises.title: Inner voice / outer voice
freestyleExercises.instruction: Speak whatever the location brings to mind. Keep going through awkward phrases. Afterwards, save one line that sounds like you.

freestyleExercises.title: Four objects, four bars
freestyleExercises.instruction: Choose four visible objects. Give each one a bar. On the next take, connect all four into one story.

freestyleExercises.title: Room to breathe
freestyleExercises.instruction: Use short phrases and comfortable pauses. Mark the pauses in your text, then try the verse at a slower tempo.

freestyleExercises.title: Flow switch
freestyleExercises.instruction: Repeat one four-bar verse. Change only the timing: steady phrases, shorter bursts, then longer pauses.

freestyleExercises.title: Metaphor forge
freestyleExercises.instruction: Choose a city detail. Write what it is, what it resembles, and what it means to you. Turn the strongest connection into a couplet.

freestyleExercises.title: Word chain
freestyleExercises.instruction: Begin with a location word. Follow associations without stopping. Use three unexpected words in a new verse.

freestyleExercises.title: Listen back without a verdict
freestyleExercises.instruction: Notice one vivid image, one clear rhythmic choice, and one phrase to revise. Describe emotional language without treating it as a diagnosis.
